Date: 2025-01-07
REMARKS
Status of the Application
Claims 1-16 are all the claims pending in the application. By this amendment, new dependent claims 14-16 have been added.
Claims 1, 4, 6-9 and 11-13 are rejected. Claims 2-3, 5 and 10 are objected to. Allowable Subject Matter
Claims 2, 3, 5, and 10 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
Applicant hold in abeyance the rewriting of these claims in independent form. Claim Rejections - 35 USC §102
Claims 1, 4, 6-9, and 11-13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No 2009/0234202 granted to Goix et al.
Claims 1 and 8
By the method of claim 1, second data is assigned "a first training label indicating that the disease is developing," even though the second data has a "second result that the disease is not developing." The second data is assigned this opposite label and assigned a weighting index "upon determining that a time interval between the first time point and the second time point is smaller than a first predetermined value."
It appears to be the Examiner's position that Goix's disclosure at para. [0438] that "statistical methods can be used to classify the sample based on the detection of the marker panels," including "[m]achine learning approaches," meets the recited "assigning, to the second
data, a first training label indicating that the disease is developing and a weighting index that is capable of taking a plurality of values according to the time interval; and performing machine learning of a model by using the second data, to which the first training label is assigned, as training data."
Applicant respectfully disagrees. Goix's general disclosure regarding classifying the sample using statistical methods cannot meet these features.
In contrast to claim 1, Goix at para. [0438] discloses that the machine learning
approaches to classification can include "weighted voting" and "k-nearest neighbors." But there is no disclosure that Goix's weighted voting is based on a time interval between first and second data points. And a k-nearest neighbors algorithm is merely based on points having close values, not a temporal closeness.
And there is no disclosure that data is assigned an opposite label (a first training label indicating that the disease is developing even though second result is that the disease is not developing) and also assigned a weighting index "upon determining that a time interval between the first time point and the second time point is smaller than a first predetermined value."
Thus, claim 1 is patentable.
Independent claim 8 is patentable for similar reasons. Claims 6 and 7 are patentable due to their dependency.
Claims 4 and 9
Independent claim 4 recites:
receiving second data including the physiological information obtained from
the first subject and a second result that the disease is not developing, the second
result being determined based on the physiological information; ...
assigning, to the second data, a first training label indicating that the disease
is developing, upon determining that a time interval between the first time point
and the second time point is smaller than a first predetermined value;
assigning, to the second data, a second training label indicating that the
disease is not developing, upon determining that the second time point is earlier
than a reference time point by a second predetermined value or more;
Much like claim 1, claim 4 also recites that data is assigned an opposite label (a first training label indicating that the disease is developing even though second result is that the disease is not developing) when "a time interval between the first time point and the second time point is smaller than a first predetermined value."
As such, claim 4 is patentable for similar reasons to those discussed above with respect to claim 1.
Claim 9 is patentable for similar reasons. Claims 11-13 are patentable at least due to their dependency.
New Claims
Applicant has added new dependent claims 14-16. These claims are patentable due to their dependency.
New dependent claims 14 and 15 recite that "the weighting index representing a degree to which teaching of the first training label is considered." See specification at para. [0035]. Goix does not teach or suggest this feature.
Claim 16 recites that "the physiological information is a physiological signal waveform." This claim is similar to original claim 6, but depends from claim 4. Goix does not teach or suggest this feature.
Conclusion
In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited. If any points remain in issue which the Examiner feels may be best resolved through a personal or telephone interview, the Examiner is kindly requested to contact the undersigned at the telephone number listed below.
The USPTO is directed and authorized to charge all required fees, except for the Issue Fee and the Publication Fee, to Deposit Account No. 19-4880. Please also credit any overpayments to said Deposit Account.
Respectfully submitted, /John M. Bird/
